$comment: The reverse index into docs/layers.json: from a library a project already
depends on, to the kiwa layer that tests it.
docs/layers.json answers 'what does this layer need'. This file answers the
question `kiwa init --detect` actually asks, which is the other way round:
here is a Cargo.toml, which layers apply.
Two kinds of entry, and they are not interchangeable:
generated  Five packages name their target libraries in peerDependencies
(auth, orm, cache, queue, ui). Those lists are the declaration;
scripts/rebuild-stack-signals.mjs copies them here and --check
fails when a peer is added without regenerating. `dapp` has the
peers but no layer, so it produces nothing.
manual     The rest declare only `vitest` or nothing at all. Their adapters
mock the framework rather than importing it, so there is nothing
here to read — but the project being tested depends on the
framework directly, and that is what gets read. Written by hand
for that reason, not because the layers are less real.
Counting the manual side by hand got it wrong twice, so it is stated by
measurement instead. Nineteen packages carry no dependency beyond `vitest`.
Ten TypeScript layers belong to them: the five `nextjs-*`, `edge-handler`,
`e2e`, `unit`, `data` and `cli`. The remaining opaque packages — hono, fresh,
solidjs, component — have no layer at all, so there is nothing to point a
signal at.
Only `next` is written so far. It is the one with evidence: 18 of the 26
`*nextjs*` examples depend on it, and one more outside that naming
(`dogfood-dapp-e2e-reorg`). The `*edge*`, `*hono*`, `*solid*` and
`*fresh*` examples carry no real dependency between them, so a signal for
those would be a guess with nothing to check it against. `unit`, `data`,
`cli` and `e2e` are not framework-shaped and no single dependency implies
them.
The boundary is not arbitrary: it lines up with the categories in
docs/libraries.json. Services are transparent, frameworks and ai-realtime are
opaque.
Precedence. A signal can point at more than one layer — `ioredis` serves both
cache and job-queue, `axum` appears in a project whose real subject is
tower-http. `strength` orders them: an `exact` signal settles the question, a
`weak` one only applies when no exact signal claimed the same layer group.
For Rust the exact signal is the kiwa-test-rs feature, because the framework
dependency alone cannot tell rust-axum from rust-tower-http — the tower-http
example depends on axum too.
This file only lists what a manifest can show. Detection never installs;
`kiwa init --detect` prints and writes .kiwa/stack.json, and `--apply` is a
separate step. A wrong guess costs a line of output.

`also` exists because one dependency can imply more than one layer. The adapter package serves the unit and the integration layer alike, and nothing in Cargo.toml or go.mod distinguishes them: rust-cargo-poc has tests/poc.rs and tests/poc_integration.rs and one kiwa-test-rs entry. Reporting only the unit layer would hide half of what the project already tests.

rust.note: Presence of the adapter means the unit layer. It may also mean the integration layer — rust-cargo-poc carries tests/poc.rs and tests/poc_integration.rs against one entry — so `also` states that as a fallback the resolver drops once a framework layer appears.
rust-tower-http-poc depends on axum as well, so this only applies when no feature said otherwise.

go.note: Presence of the adapter means the unit layer. It may also mean the integration layer — go-testing-poc carries calc_test.go and integration/client_test.go against one module — so `also` states that as a fallback the resolver drops once a framework layer appears.

typescript.note: The adapter mocks Next.js rather than importing it, so nothing in this repository's packages names `next` — but a project using Next.js depends on it directly, which is what this file reads. `exact` because the dependency settles that the project is a Next.js one. Which of the five layers applies is a separate question a manifest cannot answer: server actions, middleware, RSC, parallel routes and streaming are distinguished by file layout, not by dependencies. All five are therefore implied together, and `default` holding `nextjs-rsc` is not a claim that it is the likeliest — the resolver treats `default` and `also` alike here, since no asserted signal exists in the group to drop them.

$comment: Written by scripts/rebuild-stack-signals.mjs from the peerDependencies of the
transparent packages. `--check` fails when a peer is added without
regenerating, so a library cannot become undetectable by being forgotten.
Every peer becomes a signal. Sorting them into 'the library under test' and
'a tool used to test it' needs a judgement the generator cannot make:
`testcontainers` is a tool for orm and the subject of nothing, while
`ioredis` is the subject for cache and a tool for job-queue. An exclusion
list would have to be maintained by hand, which is the drift this file
exists to remove.
`strength` carries the distinction instead. Peers are emitted `weak`, and
`resolve` drops a weak detection once anything `exact` claims its group. A
peer that docs/layers.json names in `providers` is emitted `exact`, because
naming it there is the project's own statement that it is a subject.
`providers` and the package names are written differently on purpose —
`nextauth` against `next-auth`, `clerk` against `@clerk/backend`. The
generator reduces both to letters and digits, and also matches a scoped
package on its scope alone. Three declared providers reach no peer at all
(`keydb`, `cloudflare`, `sqs`): they are named as options the layer supports
and nothing in the repository depends on them yet.
`dapp` is skipped and the generator says so: no layer declares `kiwa-dapp`
as its consumer, so its peers have nothing to point at.
Every entry carries a `language` and applies only to manifests of that
language. It is not decoration: these are npm names, and npm names share a
namespace with Rust crate names — `redis`, `postgres` and `testcontainers`
all exist in both. An entry with no `language` matches nothing, because a
missing field means the generator is out of date and 'applies everywhere' is
the behaviour that field exists to remove.
